FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( Third Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized bv the Copper and Copper Alloys Sectional Committee had been approved by the Metallurgical Engineering Division Council. This standard was first published in 1960 and subsequently revised in 1969 and 1982. In this revision following modifications have been made: a) Requirements of tolerances on eccentricity, ovality, roundness and straightness have been included; b) Requirements of Cu-DLP and Cu-DHP grades of copper tubes have been included, as these are widely used in condensers and heat exchangers; Requirements of chemical and physical properties of Cu-DLP and Cu-DHP grades have been incorporated; 4 Requirements of mechanical properties of other existing grades have been modified; and e) Requirements of sampling and retest have been modified.

SOLIDDRAWNCOPPERANDCOPPERALLOY TUBESFORCONDENSERSANDHEAT SPECIFICATION EXCHANGERS( Third Revision )
1 SCOPE This standard covers the requirements of solid drawn ( seamless ) copper and copper alloy tubes of outside diameters 5 mm to 80 mm, both inclusive, for use in condensers and heat exchangers. 2 REFERENCES The Indian Standards listed in Annex A are necessary adju.lct to this standard. 3 TERMINOLOGY 3.1 For the purpose of this standard the following definitions as given in IS 3288 ( Part 3 ) : 1986 shall apply. 3.1.1 Seamless Tube produced 3.1.2 Tube Shell A hollow cylinder rotary piercing, or drawing into tube. produced by extrusion, subsequent casting for

AND TOLERANCES 9.2 The chemical composition shall be determined either by the method specified in IS 440 : 1963, IS 3685 : 1966 or any other established instrumental/chemical method. In case of dispute, the procedure specified in the latest edition of IS 440, IS 3685 shall be referee method. 9.3 In case of copper-nickel alloys, the method for chemical analysis may be agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer. 10.1 Mechanical Properties The tubes shall conform to the requirements mechanical properties as given in Table 2. 10.1.1 Hardness Test Hardness test shall be carried out in accordance with IS 1501 ( Part 1 ) : 1984. 10.1.2 Tensile Test A piece of tube selected for test, suitably plugged or flattened sufficiently for gripping or a strip cut from a tube, shall be tested in accordance with IS 2655 : 1964. 10.2 Flattening Test 10.2.1 The flattening test shall be carried out as per IS 2328 : 1983 on tubes in TA and 0 conditition The tubes in HB and HD condition shall be annealed before testing. 10.2.2 The test piece shall not crack when close flattened until the interior surfaces of the tube meet as shown in Fig. 1. 10.3 Drift Expanding Test 10.3.1 The drift expanding test shall be cal'ried out as per IS 2335 : 1985 on tubes in TA and 0 in HB and HD The tubes conditions. conditions shall be annealed before testing. of

8.2 Tolerances 8.2.1 The relevant tolerances on mean outside diameter, mean wall thickness, straightness, as specified in the length and roundness IS 5493 : 1981 shall be applicable for respective sizes. 8.2.2 The tolerances on ovality and eccentricity shall be as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. However no tolerance on ovality shall be specified for tubes of wall thickness up to and including 0.4 mm. 8.2.3 The tolerances on ovality, roundness and eccentricity are applicable for HB and HD conditions only. If the tubes are supplied in TA or 0 condition the tolerances should be verified before heat-treatment. 9 CHEMICAL COMPOSITION 9.1 The chemical composition shall comply with the requirement as given in Table 1.

10.4 Non-Destructive Testing 10.4.0 All tubes shall meet the requirements of eddy-current and hydrostatic/pneumatic test. 10.4.1 Eddy-Current Test Each tube shall be subjected to the eddy-current test in accordance with IS 11612 : 1984. Tubes shall be tested in HD condition prior to the final annealing or heat treatment unless otherwise agreed upon by the supplier and the purchaser. 10.4.1.1 The hole size shall be as agreed between the supplier and the purchaser. 10.4.2 Hydrostatic Test In addition to eddy current test, each tube shall be subjected to an internal hydrostatic test pressure of 7 MPa or the value given by the following formula, whichever is less, unless otherwise agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. When subjected to the test for a minimum period of 5 seconds, the tube shall not show any sign of weeping or leaking. in

FIG. 1

11 SAMPLING CONFORMITY

AND CRITERIA FOR

11.0 Unless otherwise agreed to between the and the supplier, the following purchaser procedure of sampling and criteria for conformity should be followed for acceptance of a lot. 11.1 Lot In any consignment tubes of the same grade, size, thickness and condition shall be grouped together to constitute a lot of 300 tubes or 1000 kg ( whichever is higher ) or part thereof, 11.2 Dimensional Tolerances From each lot, ten tubes shall be selected at random and tested for length, outside diameter and wall thickness. No failure shall occur if the lot is to be accepted under this clause. 11.3 Chemical Composition, Mechanical Properties, Flattening Test and Drift Expanding Test From the lot found acceptable for dimensions, one test shall be conducted for each of the chemical composition, mechanical properties, flattening test and drift expanding test requirements as given in the specification. The lot shall be accepted if the samples tested meet the requirements of the specification for these tests. 11.4 Eddy-current Pneumatic Test Test and Hyrostatic Test/

Each tube shall be tested to a minimum internal air pressure of 35 N/cm2 for a minimun period of 5 seconds without showing any sign of leakage while immersed in water. 10.5 Microscopic Examination ( For TA and 0 Conditions only ) in longitudinal direction of tubes Samples selected for the test shall be subjected to microscopic examination in accordance with IS 4748 : 1988 at a magnification of 75 x and shall show uniform and complete recrystallization with an average grain size of 0.010 to Maximum grain size shall not 0.050 mm. exceed 0.050 mm. 10.6 Ammonia Vapour Cracking Test/Mercurous Nitrate Test ( For TA and 0 Conditions only ) agreement between the purchaser and tubes of TA and 0 conditions may be subjected to the ammonia vapour cracking test tests as per 10.6.1 nitrate or mercurous and 10.6.2.
supplier,
10.6.0 By

10.6.1 Ammonia Vapour Cracking Test
10.6.1.1 Dissolve 107 gm of ammonium chloride Place the glass in 1 000 ml distilled water. Add electrode of a pH meter in the solution. flakes small quantities of sodium hydroxide until pH value of 10 is obtained.

10.6.1.2 Degrease 150 mm length of tube in the condition as offered for inspection. Pickle in a 10 percent sulphuric acid solution and then Suspend the sample in a wash and dry. desiccator above the solution for a period of 24 hours with the lid closed. After 24 hours remove the samples, pickle lightly in 10 percent sulphuric acid solution and examine for crack. Slight drifting or flattening may be resorted to easily reveal any cracks. Cracking associated with the sawn ends of the tube samples shall be ignored. Should any specimen fail to meet the requirements of this test, all the tubes represented by the sample shall be treated as rejected. However, these tubes could be withdrawn and resubmitted for inspection after further heat treatment. 10.6.2 Mercurous Nitrate Test The mercurous nitrate test shall be carried out in accordance with IS 2305 : 1988 and shall not show any sign of cracking. 4

Each tube shall be tested for eddy-current test and hydrostatic/pneumatic test as prescribed in 10.4. 11.5 Microscopic Examination lot shall be tested for

If both the test results satisfy the relevant requirements, the lot shall be considered as conforming to the specification; otherwise not. for

If the test results on any sample for bend test, tensile test, flattening test and drift expanding test fails to satisfy the requirements specified in this standard, two more tests shall be done If both the test results for that test only. satisfy the relevant requirements; the lot shall be considered as conforming to specification, otherwise not. 11.7.3 Microscopic Examination/Ammonia

13.1 Boxes containing tubes shall be suitably marked with the following details: a) Lot Number, b) Grade, c) Condition, d) Size, and e) Indication of the source of manufacture.
13.2 Standard Marking 13.2.1 The material may also the Standard Mark.

Should any specimen fail under above tests, all the tubes represented by the sample shall rejected. However, they may be stand resubmitted for inspection after appropriate heat treatment. 12 PACKING The tubes shall be suitably covered with a avoid polyethylene sheet and packed to movements and rubbing. The tube ends shall be protected by proper inserts to avoid damage during handling and transit. Each package shall be of convenient weight for ease of handling and shall not exceed 1 000 kg ( gross ). The bottom of the packing case shall be rigid to enable the tubes to maintain straightness.

13.2.2 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards, Act 1986 and the Rules and Regumade thereunder. lations The details of conditions under which the licence for the use of Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 14 TEST CERTIFICATE The manufacttrrer/supplier should provide test each consignment giving certificate information like grade, lot number, condition, size, and thickness and corresponding chemical composition and physical properties.
